communication___index.md-54-   - **Use inclusive language**: Review AI outputs for bias and ensure they align with our Diversity, Inclusion & Belonging value.
communication___index.md-55-   - **Keep broadcasts short**: AI tools can generate verbose and repetitive content. Edit for brevity and clarity, especially in one-to-many communications. Optimize for efficiency for the right group. Consider your audience's time when deciding what to share.
communication___index.md:56:1. **Protect confidential information**: Be aware of [Data Classification Standards](/handbook/security/policies_and_standards/data-classification-standard/) for the data and AI tooling you're using. Use only approved internal tools for sensitive content.
communication___index.md-57-1. **Maintain authenticity**: Ensure your communications reflect genuine human judgment and align with our values. This is especially important in customer interactions and when providing feedback.
communication___index.md-58-1. **Don't use AI disclosure to deflect responsibility**: Consider your intent before mentioning AI use. Transparency should add value, not serve as a disclaimer reducing your accountability. If you're mentioning it to hedge against errors, your content may not be ready to share.
--

security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md-6-## Purpose
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md-7-
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md:8:The Data Classification Standard defines data type and categories and provides the associated Data Classification of each for the purposes of determining the level of protection to be applied to GitLab and Customer's Data throughout its lifecycle.
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md-9-
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md-10-## Scope
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md-11-
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md:12:The Data Classification Standard applies to all GitLab team members, contractors, consultants, vendors and other service providers that handle, manage, store or transmit GitLab data.
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md-13-
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md-14-## Roles & Responsibilities
--
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md-22-### GitLab Responsibilities
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md-23-
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md:24:- GitLab team members, contractors, consultants, vendors and all other service providers acting on behalf of GitLab are required to review and understand this data classification standard, and how to handle data according to the classification levels below unless otherwise noted.
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md-25-
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md:26:- Data Owners shall determine the classification of data in accordance with this standard. The Data Classification Index (internal only) provides a list of various types of data and their classification level. If you cannot identify the data element or are uncertain of the risk associated with the data and how it should be classified and handled, please contact the Security Risk team in Slack via @security-risk.

security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md:28:[Omitted long matching line]

security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md-30-### Customer Responsibilities
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md-31-
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md:32:- GitLab customers are responsible for managing their own data, to include identification and classification according to their own internal requirements. GitLab handles our Customer's Data internally according to our non-disclosure obligations written in our Mutual Non Disclosure Agreement and the classifications identified in this standard.
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md-33-
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md-34-## Standard
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md-35-
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md:36:### Data Classification Definitions
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md-37-
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md-38-- Personal Data: Any data, individually or when combined with other data, that identifies, relates to, describes or is reasonably capable of being associated with or linked to an identifiable natural person (a 'data subject'), whether directly or indirectly.
--

security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md-96-- Personal Data
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md-97-  - Any vendor who is in possession of any form of Personal Data must have appropriate contractual terms that address GitLab data protection requirements (e.g. a Data Processing Agreement).
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md:98:  - If Personal Data comprises a part of the data set to be processed, then the data classification for that data set should be Orange and the classification cannot be Yellow or Green, even if the majority of the data set is Yellow or Green data.
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md:99:  - The source of the Personal Data should not change its classification to a level below Orange since Personal data gathered from public sources is not exempt from protection under certain data protection laws.
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md:100:  - If you have doubts as to whether something is Personal Data, please see an exhaustive list of Personal Data elements in the [Data Classification Index](https://internal.gitlab.com/handbook/security/policies_and_standards/standards/data_classification/) (internal only)

security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md:139:### Data Classification Standards
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md-140-
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md-141-#### Credentials and access tokens are classified at the same level as the data they protect
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md-142-
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md:143:Credentials such as passwords, personal access tokens, encryption keys, and session cookies derive their classification from the highest classification of the data they protect.
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md-144-
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md:145:##### Combinations of data types may result in a higher system classification level
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md-146-
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md:147:If there is more than one data type residing in a system, the system should be classified at the highest data classification level of the data being stored, transmitted or processed on that system.
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md-148-
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md-149-##### Labeling
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md-150-
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md:151:There is currently no internal requirement to label data according to this standard, however labels are encouraged. By labeling data according to classification level, individuals can quickly refer to this policy for proper handling.
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md-152-
security__policies_and_standards__data-classification-standard.md-153-## Exceptions
--

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role  | Responsibility |
|-----------|-----------|
| GitLab Team Members | Responsible for adhering to the requirements outlined in this standard |
| Data Owners | Responsible for approving exceptions to this standard for their owned data types. These are generally the Business Owners of a system. |
| Security and Legal (Code Owners) | Responsible for approving significant changes and exceptions to this standard |

### GitLab Responsibilities

- GitLab team members, contractors, consultants, vendors and all other service providers acting on behalf of GitLab are required to review and understand this data classification standard, and how to handle data according to the classification levels below unless otherwise noted.

- Data Owners shall determine the classification of data in accordance with this standard. The Data Classification Index (internal only) provides a list of various types of data and their classification level. If you cannot identify the data element or are uncertain of the risk associated with the data and how it should be classified and handled, please contact the Security Risk team in Slack via @security-risk.

- To maintain our culture of security, transparency and to minimize the risk to our sensitive data and our customers, GitLab team members are required to complete Data Classification Training as part of GitLab's [Security Awareness Training](/handbook/security/security-assurance/governance/sec-training/) to help understand the different types of data at GitLab and how to keep it [SAFE](/handbook/legal/safe-framework/). Training is available via [LevelUp](https://levelup.edcast.com/), GitLab's internal learning platform.
